title: Rotational motion
competency: Describe rotation with angular displacement, velocity and acceleration, use the rotational equations and relate them to linear motion.

keywords.def: The angle a body turns through, Δθ = θ_f − θ₀, in radians.
How fast the angle changes: ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s.
How fast the angular velocity changes: α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s².
Angular velocity changes by the same amount every second.
The velocity of a point on a turning body, along the tangent to its circle: v = ωr.
The rate of change of tangential speed: a = rα.

en.text: In a rigid body every particle turns through the same angle. Angular displacement Δθ is measured in radians (1 rev = 2π rad = 360°). Angular velocity ω = Δθ/Δt in rad/s; angular acceleration α = Δω/Δt in rad/s². The direction of ω follows the right-hand rule; α points along ω when speeding up and opposite when slowing down.

am.text: በጠንካራ አካል ሁሉም ቅንጣቶች እኩል ማዕዘን ይዞራሉ። ω = Δθ/Δt (rad/s)፣ α = Δω/Δt (rad/s²)። 1 ዙር = 2π ራዲያን = 360°።

screens.title: Merry-go-round
screens.ask: Hana sits near the centre of a merry-go-round; Dawit sits at the edge. In one second, who turns through the bigger angle?
screens.after:
The whole ride is rigid, so every point turns through the same angle in the same time.
Dawit's circle is bigger, but the angle is the same.
Radius changes the distance moved, not the angle.

screens.title: Rotation of a rigid body
paras: A rigid body keeps its shape as it turns.
Every particle moves in a circle around the axis.
All particles turn through the same angle.

screens.title: Degrees, radians, turns
screens.ask: Turn the wheel. See the same angle in three units.
screens.note: 360° = 2π rad ≈ 6.28 rad = 1 rev. Always use radians in s = rθ and v = ωr.

screens.title: Angular velocity and acceleration
paras: Average angular velocity: ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s.
Average angular acceleration: α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s².
Right-hand rule: curl your fingers with the rotation. Your thumb points along ω.
Speeding up: α points the same way as ω.
Slowing down: α points opposite to ω.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The angle a body turns through, Δθ = θ_f − θ₀, in radians.
How fast the angle changes: ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s.
How fast the angular velocity changes: α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s².

screens.text: Units of angle: which can NOT be a unit of angular displacement?
screens.why:
Angular displacement is an angle.
Degree, radian and revolution all measure angles.
rpm means revolutions per minute: angle ÷ time.
So rpm measures angular velocity, not an angle.
screens.clue: One of these has "per minute" in it.

screens.ask: Average angular acceleration: a wheel speeds up from 30 rad/s to 50 rad/s in 2 s. α = ___ rad/s²
screens.why:
Formula: α = Δω/Δt.
Δω = 50 − 30 = 20 rad/s.
α = 20 rad/s ÷ 2 s = 10 rad/s².

screens.ask: Average angular velocity: same wheel (30 → 50 rad/s, constant α). ω_av = ___ rad/s
screens.why:
With constant α, ω_av = (ω₀ + ω_f)/2.
Substitute: (30 + 50)/2 = 80/2.
Result: 40 rad/s.
(The book's Example 2.5 asks for this but computes α.)

screens.ask: Angular velocity of a clock: the second hand has ω ≈ ___ rad/s (3 decimal places)
screens.why:
The second hand makes one turn in 60 s.
One turn = 2π rad = 6.283 rad.
ω = Δθ/Δt = 6.283 ÷ 60.
Result: ω ≈ 0.105 rad/s.
screens.clue: How long is one turn of the second hand?

screens.text: Direction of α (right-hand rule): a wheel turns counterclockwise in the xy plane and is slowing down. α points along
screens.why:
Curl right-hand fingers counterclockwise in the xy plane: the thumb points +z.
So ω is along +z.
Slowing down means α is opposite to ω.
So α points along −z.

screens.ask: Changing rpm to rad/s: a fan turns at 600 rpm. That is ≈ ___ rad/s (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Step 1: rev/min → rev/s: 600 ÷ 60 = 10 rev/s.
Step 2: rev → rad: 1 rev = 2π rad.
ω = 10 × 2π = 20π ≈ 62.8 rad/s.
Trap: forgetting ÷60 gives 3770 rad/s.

ideas.name: Equations of rotation with constant α

en.text: With constant angular acceleration the rotation equations copy the linear ones: replace s by θ, v by ω and a by α. So ω_f = ω₀ + αt, Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt², ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ and ω_av = (ω₀ + ω_f)/2. Angles must be in radians.

am.text: ቋሚ α ሲኖር የመዞሪያ እኩልታዎች ከቀጥታ እንቅስቃሴ ጋር ይመሳሰላሉ፡ ω_f = ω₀ + αt፣ Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt²፣ ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ።

screens.title: Spin a wheel
screens.ask: Set ω₀, α and t. See the angle turned.
screens.note: Make α negative: the wheel slows down. If ω_f goes below zero, the wheel has stopped and turned back.

screens.title: Linear and angular motion
paras: The two sets of equations match one to one.

screens.title: Key word
defs: Angular velocity changes by the same amount every second.

screens.title: Match each linear quantity to its angular partner
screens.why:
Displacement s ↔ angle θ.
Velocity v ↔ angular velocity ω.
Acceleration a ↔ angular acceleration α.
So v_f = v₀ + at becomes ω_f = ω₀ + αt.
screens.clue: Each linear letter has a Greek partner.
screens.text: Linear and angular equations: match each linear quantity to its angular partner.

screens.ask: Angle turned with constant α: a wheel starts at 10 rad/s with α = 2.5 rad/s². In 30 s it turns ___ rad
screens.why:
Formula: Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt².
Substitute: Δθ = 10 × 30 + ½ × 2.5 × 30².
= 300 + ½ × 2.5 × 900 = 300 + 1125.
Result: 1425 rad (≈ 227 rev).

screens.ask: Final angular velocity: same wheel (10 rad/s, α = 2.5 rad/s²). At t = 20 s, ω = ___ rad/s
screens.why:
Formula: ω_f = ω₀ + αt.
Substitute: ω_f = 10 + 2.5 × 20.
Result: 10 + 50 = 60 rad/s.

screens.ask: Angular velocity after a number of turns: a car wheel starts at 6 rad/s with α = 3 rad/s². After 100 rev, ω ≈ ___ rad/s (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
No time is given, so use ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ.
Convert: Δθ = 100 × 2π = 628 rad.
Substitute: ω_f² = 6² + 2 × 3 × 628 = 36 + 3768 = 3804.
ω_f = √3804 ≈ 61.7 rad/s.
Trap: do not square α (the book's slip), and do not use rev.
screens.clue: Change rev to rad, then use ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ. Do not square α.

screens.ask: Stopping angle: a wheel turning at 3 rad/s slows at 5 rad/s². It turns ___ rad before it stops
screens.why:
Use ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ with ω_f = 0 and α = −5 rad/s².
0 = 3² + 2(−5)Δθ = 9 − 10Δθ.
Δθ = 9 ÷ 10 = 0.9 rad.
Trap: using α = +5 gives a negative angle.

screens.ask: Angular acceleration from rpm: a wheel goes from 200 rpm to 600 rpm in 8 s. α ≈ ___ rad/s² (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Δω = 600 − 200 = 400 rpm.
Convert: 400 × 2π ÷ 60 = 41.9 rad/s.
Formula: α = Δω/Δt = 41.9 ÷ 8.
Result: α ≈ 5.24 rad/s².
Trap: 400 ÷ 8 = 50 is in rpm per second, not rad/s².

en.text: A point at distance r from the axis moves along an arc s = rθ. Its tangential speed is v = ωr and its tangential acceleration is a = rα. Every point has the same ω and α, but points farther out move faster. θ must be in radians.

am.text: ከዘንጉ r ርቀት ላይ ያለ ነጥብ s = rθ ይጓዛል፤ v = ωr፣ a = rα። ሁሉም ነጥቦች እኩል ω አላቸው፤ ሩቅ ያሉት ግን ፈጣን ናቸው።

screens.title: Who moves faster?
screens.ask: Back on the merry-go-round: Hana near the centre, Dawit at the edge. Who moves faster in metres per second?
screens.after:
Both turn through the same angle each second: the same ω.
But v = ωr, and Dawit is at a bigger r.
So Dawit covers more metres each second.

screens.title: Arc, speed and acceleration
paras: Arc length: s = rθ, with θ in radians.
The velocity is always along the tangent to the circle.
All points share ω and α. v and a grow with r.

screens.title: Edge or centre?
screens.ask: Keep ω fixed and move outward. Watch the speed.
screens.note: Same ω for Hana and Dawit. Double r: double v.

screens.title: A bicycle wheel
steps: r = 30 cm = 0.3 m; 2000 rev in 5 min = 300 s.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The velocity of a point on a turning body, along the tangent to its circle: v = ωr.
The rate of change of tangential speed: a = rα.

screens.text: Speed on a turning wheel, true or false: all points on a turning wheel have the same linear speed.
screens.why:
All points share the same ω.
Linear speed is v = ωr.
A point on the rim (big r) moves faster than one near the axle.
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: Compare a point on the rim with one near the axle.

screens.ask: Tangential speed: a bicycle wheel (radius 40 cm) turns at 18 rad/s. The bicycle's speed is ___ m/s
screens.why:
Formula: v = ωr.
Convert: r = 40 cm = 0.4 m.
Substitute: v = 18 rad/s × 0.4 m.
Result: 7.2 m/s.
Trap: using 40 cm gives 720, a unit error.

screens.ask: Turns of a pulley: a rope on a pulley of radius 50 cm lifts a bucket 20 m. The pulley turns ≈ ___ rev (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Rope length = arc length: s = rΔθ.
Δθ = s/r = 20 m ÷ 0.5 m = 40 rad.
Revolutions = 40 ÷ 2π = 40 ÷ 6.283.
Result: ≈ 6.37 rev. (The book prints 6.34.)

screens.ask: Tangential acceleration: a disc goes from rest to 20 rad/s in 4 s. A point 40 cm from the centre has a = ___ m/s²
screens.why:
Step 1: α = Δω/Δt = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 rad/s².
Step 2: a = rα = 0.4 m × 5 rad/s².
Result: a = 2 m/s².
Check: at 20 cm it would be 1 m/s².
screens.clue: Find α first, then a = rα.

screens.ask: Angular velocity of a pulley: radius 20 cm, lifts a bucket 10 m in 5 s. ω_av = ___ rad/s
screens.why:
Δθ = s/r = 10 m ÷ 0.2 m = 50 rad.
ω = Δθ/Δt = 50 rad ÷ 5 s.
Result: 10 rad/s.
Check: v = 10/5 = 2 m/s, and ωr = 10 × 0.2 = 2 m/s ✓

screens.ask: Angle from arc length: a particle moves 2.50 m along a circle of radius 1.50 m. It turns ≈ ___ rad (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Formula: θ = s/r (θ in radians).
Substitute: θ = 2.50 m ÷ 1.50 m.
Result: θ ≈ 1.67 rad (≈ 95.5°).

screens.ask: Angular acceleration of car wheels: a car speeds up from 20 m/s to 24 m/s in 5 s. Its wheels (radius 40 cm) have α = ___ rad/s²
screens.why:
Linear acceleration of the rim: a = Δv/Δt = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8 m/s².
Link: a = rα, so α = a/r.
α = 0.8 ÷ 0.4 = 2 rad/s².
screens.clue: Find the linear acceleration of the rim first.

items.text: Exercise 2.2 Q1, true or false: when a wheel turns about a fixed axis, all points have the same angular speed.
items.why:
The wheel is rigid.
Every point turns through the same angle in the same time.
So every point has the same ω.
(Their linear speeds v = ωr differ.)

items.ask: Exercise 2.2 Q6 b, number of turns: a wheel goes from 200 rpm to 600 rpm in 8 s. It makes ≈ ___ revolutions (1 decimal place)
items.why:
With constant α, use the average rate.
ω_av = (200 + 600)/2 = 400 rpm = 400 ÷ 60 = 6.67 rev/s.
Turns = ω_av × t = 6.67 × 8.
Result: ≈ 53.3 rev.

test.ask: Units of angle: 1 revolution = ___ rad (2 decimal places)
Angular acceleration: a wheel goes from rest to 12 rad/s in 4 s. α = ___ rad/s²
test.why:
Formula: α = Δω/Δt.
α = (12 − 0) ÷ 4.
Result: 3 rad/s².

test.ask: Angle turned: ω₀ = 4 rad/s, α = 2 rad/s². In 5 s the wheel turns ___ rad
test.why:
Formula: Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt².
= 4 × 5 + ½ × 2 × 5².
= 20 + 25 = 45 rad.

test.ask: Tangential speed: a wheel of radius 0.3 m turns at 25 rad/s. A point on the rim moves at ___ m/s
test.why:
Formula: v = ωr.
v = 25 × 0.3.
Result: 7.5 m/s.

test.ask: Stopping angle: a wheel at 8 rad/s slows at 2 rad/s². It turns ___ rad before stopping
test.why:
Use ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ with ω_f = 0, α = −2.
0 = 64 − 4Δθ.
Δθ = 64 ÷ 4 = 16 rad.

notes.text: Example 2.5 asks for the average angular velocity but computes the angular acceleration (10 rad/s²). Average ω = (30 + 50)/2 = 40 rad/s. The lesson asks for both.
Example 2.7: the substitution squares α ("2 × (3 rad/s²)² × 628"). It should be 2 × 3 × 628. The answer 61.68 rad/s is right.
Example 2.10: 5 min = 300 s, not 3000 s. The answer 6.67 rev/s needs 300 s.
Example 2.12: the line "Δs = 0.4 m × 18 rad/s" should read v = 0.4 × 18.
Figure 2.10 label: the rotation shown is counterclockwise, not clockwise.
